name: Heath
summary: A sleep wearable in development. It follows your sleep through the night and settles the restless moments, so you get the most restorative sleep and recover best.
problem: Sleep turns restless many times a night. Most of these moments do not wake you, but they cost restorative sleep.

how_it_works.description: It follows your sleep, all night.
It catches the moment sleep starts to thin.
A little warmth, a low tone or a light touch. Then quiet.

signals_planned.description: A small rise in skin warmth
signals_planned.evidence: Warming the skin by 0.4 C deepened sleep; in older adults, early waking fell from 58% to 4%.
Slow rocking cut arousals in deep sleep by 60%.

signals_planned.description: Soft tones in time with slow waves
signals_planned.evidence: Soft tones in rhythm with slow waves made them stronger and longer.

evidence_note: These studies tested the signals in sleep labs, not Heath. Heath's own results have not been published.

why_it_matters.fact: Healthy sleepers stir about 11 times an hour in their twenties and about 22 by their fifties.
why_it_matters.source: Bonnet & Arand, J Clin Sleep Med, 2007

why_it_matters.fact: Older adults with the most fragmented sleep were 1.5 times as likely to develop Alzheimer's.
Deep sleep is about a fifth of the night before 25; after 35 it falls under 5%, in a study of 149 healthy men.

waitlist.how: Email form at the end of the home page; the 'Join the waitlist' button at the top leads to it
waitlist.agent_guidance: Ask the person for consent before submitting their email.

disclaimers: Not a medical device; does not diagnose or treat any condition
Features are planned and may change
The one-night sleep chart on the home page is an illustration, not a recording
